questions.title: Getting your ball out of a bunker when there is a puddle or ground is too wet
questions.question: If your ball is in a bunker and there is a big puddle or very wet ground (abnormal condition), what do the rules say if you want to move your ball out of the bunker to play it?

choices.text: You can drop the ball outside the bunker with no extra shots.
You can drop the ball outside the bunker, but you have to add one penalty stroke.
You can put the ball anywhere outside the bunker with no extra shots.
You are not allowed to move your ball outside the bunker.

questions.explanation: If you need to move your ball out of the bunker because of a puddle or wet ground, you must count one extra shot (penalty stroke).

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A sandy area on the golf course, usually shaped like a big pit or hole.
A chance to move your ball to a better spot when something unfair is stopping you (like a puddle).
Something on the course that is not usually there, like water in a bunker or ground that is too soft.
An extra shot you must add to your score when you take a special option in the rules.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids a bunker with water in it and use a second ball to show dropping outside the bunker and remembering to count an extra shot.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think they never have to add any shots when moving out of a bunker.
They might believe they can put the ball anywhere they want outside the bunker.

questions.title: Dropping outside a bunker due to abnormal conditions
questions.question: If you take relief outside a bunker from an abnormal course condition in the bunker, what must you do according to the Rules?

choices.text: Drop outside the bunker without penalty
Drop outside the bunker and add one penalty stroke
Place the ball anywhere outside the bunker without penalty
You cannot take relief outside the bunker

questions.explanation: If you take relief outside the bunker for abnormal course conditions, you must add a one-stroke penalty.
